<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

% Determine grid size
nr(NR) :- NR = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(NC) :- NC = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).

    outside(R1, C1),
    delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1 + DR,
    C2 = C1 + DC,
    input(R2, C2, V),
    V != 8.

output_cell(R, C) :-

    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

   input(DR, DC, _),

% Determine grid dimensions
nr(NR) :- NR = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(NC) :- NC = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Border predicate
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = NR-1.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = 0.

% Adjacent offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non‑wall cells (colour != W)
non_wall(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != W.

% Outside region: border cells that are non‑wall, and flood‑fill through non‑wall cells
outside(R,C) :- border(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != W.
outside(R2,C2) :-
    outside(R1,C1),
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1+DR,
    C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2,C2,V),
    V != W.

% Count border colours and interior colours for each colour
colour_present(C) :- input(_,_,C).

% Determine wall colour: a colour that occurs on the border and also occurs somewhere interior
wall(W) :-
    border_colour(W),
    #count{R : input(R,_,W), not border(R,_) } > 0,
    #count{R : input(R,_,W), border(R,_) } > 0.

border_colour(W) :- border(R,C), input(R,C,W).

% Determine filler colour: the smallest colour (1..9) that does not appear in the input and is not the wall colour
missing_colour(M) :- color(M), not colour_present(M), M != 0, M != W.

filler(F) :- color(F), missing_colour(F), not missing_colour(M) :- color(M), M > F.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Determine grid dimensions (if needed for border calculations)
nr(NR) :- NR = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(NC) :- NC = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Border cells (any cell on the outer edge)
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = NR-1.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = NC-1.

% 4‑connected neighbours
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% -------------------------------------------------
% Determine the wall colour: a colour that appears both on the border
% and also somewhere inside the grid.
wall(W) :-
    #count{R,C : border(R,C), input(R,C,W)} > 0,
    #count{R,C : input(R,C,W), not border(R,C)} > 0.

% Determine which colours appear in the input
colour_present(C) :- input(_,_,C).

% Determine colours that are missing (not present) and are non‑zero and not the wall colour
missing(M) :- color(M), not colour_present(M), M != 0, M != W.

% The filler colour is the smallest missing colour (there will be exactly one)
filler(F) :- missing(F), #count{R : missing(R), R < F} = 0.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Outside region: start from border cells whose colour is not the wall,
% and flood‑fill through cells whose colour is not the wall.
outside(R,C) :- border(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != W.
outside(R2,C2) :-
    outside(R1,C1),
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1+DR,
    C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2,C2,V),
    V != W.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Output constraints.
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% Exactly one colour for every output cell
1 { output(R, C, Col) : color(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% 1. Wall cells stay wall colour
:- output(R, C, Col), input(R, C, W), Col != W.

% 2. Zero cells that can reach the border stay zero

% 3. Zero cells that are enclosed become the filler colour

% 4. Non‑zero, non‑wall cells keep their original colour

% 5. Forbid the filler colour in any other cell

% 6. For each colour Cc (0..9) forbid that colour for interior zero cells
% (the only colour that is not forbidden is the filler colour F)

% Determine grid dimensions
nr(NR) :- NR = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(NC) :- NC = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Border cells
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = NR-1.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = NC-1.

outside(R2,C2) :-
    outside(R1,C1),
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1+DR,
    C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2,C2,V),

% Grid dimensions
nr(NR) :- NR = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(NC) :- NC = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Border cells
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = NR-1.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = NC-1.

% Adjacent offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Outside region (cells reachable from border through cells that are not 8)
outside(R,C) :- border(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 8.
outside(R2,C2) :-
    outside(R1,C1),
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1+DR,
    C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2,C2,V),
    V != 8.

output(R, C, 2), input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), 2 != 3.

nr(NR) :- NR = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(NC) :- NC = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Border cells (any cell on the grid edge)
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = NR-1.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = NC-1.

% 4‑connected neighbourhood
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Outside region:
%   start from border cells whose colour is not 8
%   and flood‑fill through cells whose colour is not 8
outside(R,C) :- border(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 8.
outside(R2,C2) :-
    outside(R1,C1),
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1+DR,
    C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2,C2,V),
    V != 8.

% Constraint: for any non‑zero cell the output colour must equal the input colour
output(R, C, Col), input(R, C, V), V != 0, Col != V.

% Count rows and columns
nr(NR) :- NR = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(NC) :- NC = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Neighborhood offsets
delta(0,1).
delta(0,-1).
delta(1,0).
delta(-1,0).

% Border cells
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = NR-1.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = NC-1.

% Outside region (start + flood fill)
outside(R,C) :- border(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 8.
outside(R2,C2) :-
    outside(R1,C1),
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1 + DR,
    C2 = C1 + DC,
    input(R2,C2,V),
    V != 8.

% Allowed colors predicate ok(R,C,Color)
ok(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.
ok(R,C,0) :- input(R,C,0), outside(R,C).
ok(R,C,3) :- input(R,C,0), not outside(R,C).

% Output cell definition
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% Exactly one color for each output cell
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(0..9) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Enforce that the chosen color is allowed for the cell
:- output(R, C, Color), not ok(R, C, Color).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Grid dimensions
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
nr(NR) :- NR = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(NC) :- NC = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  4‑connected neighbourhood (used for the flood‑fill)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
delta(0,1).
delta(0,-1).
delta(1,0).
delta(-1,0).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Border cells (any cell on the outer rim)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), R = NR-1.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = 0.
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,_), C = NC-1.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Outside region:
%   – start from border cells whose colour is not 8
%   – flood‑fill through cells that are not 8
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
outside(R,C) :- border(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 8.
outside(R2,C2) :-
    outside(R1,C1),
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1 + DR,
    C2 = C1 + DC,
    input(R2,C2,V),
    V != 8.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Allowed colour for each cell
%   – non‑zero cells keep their own colour
%   – zero cells that are reachable from the border stay 0
%   – zero cells that are enclosed become 3
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
ok(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.
ok(R,C,0) :- input(R,C,0), outside(R,C).
ok(R,C,3) :- input(R,C,0), not outside(R,C).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Output cell definition (every input cell becomes an output cell)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Exactly one colour for each output cell
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(0..9) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  The chosen colour must be the allowed colour for the cell
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
:- output(R, C, Color), not ok(R, C, Color).
